Subject: LyraWorks — Notice: temporary throughput ramp affecting hosted inference (June 18)

Hi Sam —

Quick heads up: around 08:40 UTC this morning we observed a sustained ramp in token throughput from a subset of LyraWorks routes which pushed several inference pools above their autoscaling thresholds. That triggered a short period of increased queuing and elevated p95/p99 latencies for calls to the hosted-generation endpoints you use (model: redwood/xy-large).

What happened so far:
- Impact window: ~08:40 — 09:05 UTC (we mitigated before a longer outage)
- Symptoms: transient p99 increase (~3-4x normal), occasional 503s for long streaming sessions
- Immediate mitigation: we scaled a reserved burst pool and enabled region fallback to NW-US to relieve pressure

We're actively investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline and corrective actions. For now:
- If you see elevated errors or can correlate customer-facing issues, please reply with timestamps and request IDs and we'll prioritize them.
- We're preparing a short post-incident note and a status page entry (link to follow).

Attachments: debug_trace_0618.log (engine trace), autoscaler-report-0618.pdf (summary)

Apologies for the disruption — I know this is disruptive for your users. We'll share a full update within the next 6 hours and loop in engineering for an RCA invite.

Hi team —

Root cause (initial): our autoscaler experienced a short-lived race when concurrent scale-up signals were processed for the same allocation group. Two things combined: a) the scaling decision queue backed up under a transient surge, and b) an edge condition in the scale-commit path caused one of the new nodes to not join the pool immediately. That resulted in delayed capacity becoming available and queued requests hitting p99 latency and a few 503s while the fallback logic cycled.

What we did (mitigation applied ~09:05 UTC):
- Manually forced allocation of a pre-warmed burst pool to absorb the spike (temporary fix)
- Recovered the stuck node and drained queues; restored normal p95/p99 by ~09:08 UTC
- Deployed a short-term hotfix to the scale-commit path to prevent the race from recurring during similar concurrent signals

Next steps (post-incident):
- Engineering will ship a durable fix to the autoscaler control plane in the next 72 hours (planned patch + canary test)
- We'll add an additional health probe and observability event to detect the scale-commit stall faster
- CS and Sales: we can offer a retroactive credit for the window and a 1:1 RCA; happy to join a call tomorrow 10:00-11:00 PDT if that works for LyraWorks

Attached logs show the commit stall and the node rejoin sequence for the provided request-ids.

Attachments: debug_trace_0618.log (excerpted), autoscaler-report-0618.pdf
